_comment: BYS360 coverage ratchet baseline. Truthful, re-measured floor for CI's actual test scope (tests/quality -m ci_safe, then tests/integration tests/architecture tests/security tests/critical tests/services tests/migrations tests/workflow tests/release, branch=true). This value is NOT aspirational and must NEVER be raised automatically by any script -- raising it is a separate, human-reviewed action after real coverage genuinely improves. See scripts/quality/bys360_coverage_ratchet.py for enforcement logic and its docstring for the no-self-raise constraint.
_history: Phase 6 Critical Operational CI Coverage Expansion (2026-07-27): tests/migrations (33), tests/workflow (7) and tests/release (6) -- 46 tests total -- were added to the CI-enforced coverage scope. 0 cross-scope duplicate node IDs against the rest of the workflow or each other; each folder stable across 2 isolated runs + 1 combined run (46/46, 0 failed); adds only ~8% to this step's runtime. tests/migrations runs real Alembic upgrade()/downgrade() against an isolated in-memory SQLite engine (contributes ~0% to app/ coverage directly, but is retained as a required correctness gate, not for coverage credit). Combined coverage measured twice, identically, at 23.386063716089716%. Previous baseline (CI Coverage Scope Policy Closure, services-only, 2026-07-27) was combined_pct=23.27 -- kept in _history for continuity, not reused as the active floor. Prior to that (Campaign 1B, 2026-07-24) was combined_pct=18.85, see previous_baseline below.
measured_by: BYS360 Phase 6 - Critical Operational CI Coverage Expansion

previous_baseline.measured_by: BYS360 Phase 6 - CI Coverage Scope Policy Closure
previous_baseline.scope: tests/quality (ci_safe) + tests/integration + tests/architecture + tests/security + tests/critical + tests/services (migrations/workflow/release NOT included)

environment.os: Windows 11 (worktree measurement; CI runner is ubuntu-latest -- see tolerance note in ratchet script)

commands: python -m pytest tests/integration tests/architecture tests/security tests/critical tests/services tests/migrations tests/workflow tests/release --cov=app --cov-append --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=xml:reports/quality/coverage.xml --cov-fail-under=0 --tb=short -q

repeatability.note: Two independent full runs of the new combined command produced an identical measurement (deterministic given no test randomization is in use). The recorded combined_pct is the true measured value, consistent with lines_covered/lines_valid/branches_covered/branches_valid (see tests/quality/test_bys360_coverage_ratchet.py::test_committed_baseline_counts_are_internally_consistent); the sole safety margin is the pre-existing tolerance_pct field below, unchanged at 0.5 points.

tolerance_rationale: Absorbs float rounding and Windows-worktree-vs-Ubuntu-CI-runner platform noise (this baseline was measured on Windows; the actual CI runner is ubuntu-latest, which can take slightly different code paths on OS-conditional branches). Not intended to absorb a real coverage regression, which is expected to be much larger than 0.5 points in practice.
